quest.title: "The Falcon's Hunt"
quest.description: After the previous adventure, it seems that Masseira still has some favor to ask of you...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Hello. Are you ready to go?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Please follow me.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Okay... I'll wait for you.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Ah! If it isn't the esteemed Master of the Jinni, savior of my little Falcon.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: I'm embarrassed to ask but could you do me another favor? It's a hunting task.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Simply put, this is about Tadhla's coming-of-age ceremony. Please witness her growth for me.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: She could be a bit of a handful, but I promise you will be well compensated. So I'm wondering if you would like to...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, just leave it to us!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: *sigh* Really, must we...

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: It's the coming-of-age ceremony for Tadhla. I used to train the "Falcons" in the tribe personally, but now... I'm no longer as agile as I once was.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: After the previous commission, Tadhla said you have her trust. This is why I want to ask you to join in and see the Falcon's growth.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I see. I'll help.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: It's very kind of you. Please find Tadhla. She'll give you the details of this hunt.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Well then, I shall leave you alone.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Prey won't hunt themselves for us. Please go find Tadhla to learn what needs to be done.

talks.objective: Go to the Red Vulture's lair
Search for traces of the Red Vulture on the way

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Ah, you're back. Is there something else you want to talk about? Or are you just looking to chat?

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: I believe she will be a real Falcon after training with you.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Act alone or with company and hunt formidable targets, become a qualified "Falcon" for the tribe, and deal with prey and enemies...

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Simple.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Good luck with the hunt.

talks.objective: Go to the Red Vulture's lair

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: *pant* If you need my assistance... please let me know, anytime.

choices.text: You should have a rest here.
Your condition is not suitable for hunting.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: This is her lair.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Red Vultures are careful and wicked by nature. She's probably sensed the danger and fled already, leaving us an empty lair.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Now we must wait with patience.

choices.text: When will the Red Vulture return?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Not until she no longer feels in danger... Also, even if she senses our presence in the lair, she'd still be forced back here by the piercing cold of midnight.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: We will stay here and wait until midnight. Please have a rest if you are tired. I'll keep watch.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: "Fool's Gold." Red Vultures love collecting shiny stuff.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Fool's Gold"... Hmm... Sounds like Fatui's hidden treasure...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: "Fool's Gold" are things that only simpletons would believe to be valuable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon certainly wouldn't fall for that!

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Shh... You wouldn't want to have any of those. They are mostly commonplace alloys like brass and bronze that are not worth much.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: ...She hasn't returned yet. Please stay put, or she'll be alarmed.

talks.objective: Go to the hiding place and wait until the Red Vulture returns to the lair

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: ...She hasn't returned yet. Please stay put, or she'll be alarmed.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Ah, you are back. So, would you like to accept my commission?

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Very well... Now, for detail of this hunt, please talk to Tadhla.

choices.text: I have to finish something else first.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Well then, I shall leave you alone.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Please forgive me for having doubted you. You have proven that you are a talented hunter.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: We may operate under different approaches, but I must say you have amazing instincts...

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Please leave the rest to me. If you really are interested in this, I can teach you step by step.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Very well.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tadhla demonstrates how to dissect a prey. You and Paimon seem to have learned a new skill that you probably will never actually put into practice.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: \nAfter the demonstration, Tadhla shows you her hands soaked by the blood of her prey, a faint smile appearing on her lips.\nThis is the first time that she has revealed any trace of her emotions.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Hmm... The smell of blood. Good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... The smell of blood is really strong! Aren't you going to wash it off or something?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: No, because we are going to hunt the Scorpion now.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Scorpions are predators. They relish the smell of fresh blood.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: That's right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh... Alright... Paimon will hold her breath anyway!

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Do you need more rest or should we set out right now?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: It's decently chilly in this lair, our prey's meat should be able to stay overnight and not go bad... We could spend the night here to avoid the cold outside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep yep, let's get some good rest while it's still chill and cozy in here.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: It appears that the little one desires to be slothful again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, Paimon knows when she feels cold and tired! Not everyone is immune to temperature changes like you!

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Suit yourselves.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tadhla dissects the prey with great proficiency and wraps it up in a package.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: *sigh* This would be the Red Vulture's lair.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: I don't know if you're purely reckless, or highly instinctual... But we still have time.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Red Vultures are careful and wicked by nature. She's probably sensed the danger and fled already, leaving us an empty lair.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Now we must wait with patience.

choices.text: When will the Red Vulture return?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Not until she no longer feels in danger... Also, even if she senses our presence in the lair, she'd still be forced back here by the piercing cold of midnight.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: We will stay here and wait until midnight. Please have a rest if you are tired. I'll keep watch.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: "Fool's Gold." Red Vultures love collecting shiny stuff.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Fool's Gold"... Hmm... Sounds like Fatui's hidden treasure...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: "Fool's Gold" are things that only simpletons would believe to be valuable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon certainly wouldn't fall for that!

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Shh... You wouldn't want to have any of those. They are mostly commonplace alloys like brass and bronze that are not worth much.

talks.objective: Talk to Tadhla and set out together

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: You are such a talented hunter. No wonder Father commissioned you to help me with this hunt.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Please leave the rest to me. If you really are interested in this, I can teach you step by step.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Very well.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tadhla demonstrates how to dissect a prey. You and Paimon seem to have learned a new skill that you probably will never actually put into practice.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After the demonstration, Tadhla shows you her hands soaked by the blood of her prey, a faint smile appearing on her lips.\nThis is the first time that she has revealed any trace of her emotions.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Hmm... The smell of blood. Good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can smell it, too! Uh... Such a strong smell... Aren't you going to wash it off?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: No, because we are going to hunt the Scorpion now.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Scorpions are predators. They relish the smell of fresh blood.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: That's right.

response.speaker: Paimon

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Do you need more rest or should we set out right now?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: It's decently chilly in this lair, our prey's meat should be able to stay overnight and not go bad... We could spend the night here to avoid the cold outside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds good to Paimon! The temperature feels just right in here. Let's all just get some good rest for the night!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: It appears that the little one desires to be slothful again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, Paimon knows when she feels cold and tired! Not everyone is immune to temperature changes like you!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tadhla fetches some desert poplar branches and dried feces. Soon, a simple campfire is built.\nSitting and bathing in its warm light, you all share filling quantities of food and water with each other.\nWatching the campfire dancing and crackling, you find yourselves absent of any topics to discuss...

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Suit yourselves.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tadhla dissects the prey with great proficiency and wraps it up in a package.

talks.objective: Rest for a night and talk to Tadhla

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: You're back.

choices.text: Let's go and continue the hunt.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: I'll lead the way. Please follow me.

choices.text: I have some other things to do.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Suit yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Tadhla fetches some desert poplar branches and dried feces. Soon, a simple campfire is built.\nSitting and bathing in its warm light, you all share filling quantities of food and water with each other.\nWatching the campfire dancing and crackling, you find yourselves absent of any topics to discuss...

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: He is my father. I am his "Falcon."

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Did you rest well? Are we ready to go?

choices.text: Let's go and continue the hunt.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Please follow me.

choices.text: I have some other things to do. I'll be back later.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Suit yourselves.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Talking the talk is the doings of parrots. Falcons only walk the walk.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: About me...?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: There's nothing much to say about me... Are you sure you want to know more about me?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: I am a Falcon. I am only allowed to learn about my prey, not any other way around.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: So... I am sorry, but I will not betray myself to you.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Be that so? Some advice to you, child: Think for yourself.

choices.text: I want to know what kind of person I am working with.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: "Person"? No. A "Falcon"? Yes.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Please rest assured. I will not disobey you or leave you behind. It is Father who entrusted me to you.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Heh... A blind-folded Falcon. In what world would she care about how beautiful she is?

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Here we are.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Scorpions are only active under the veil of night. There is still some time before the night falls. Why don't we plan how we hunt the Scorpion?

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: First option, we can mix the secretions of Sand Grease Pupa with a few ground poisonous mushrooms. Secretions of Sand Grease Pupa should lure the Scorpion to take the bait, then ground poisonous mushrooms can paralyze the Scorpion.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: The toxin is not strong enough to kill it, but would very well suffice to immobilize it.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Or, we can mash up a mixture of Henna Berries and viper venom. Then make some poisonous bait by adding fresh meat into the mush. We fight fire with fire.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: But viper venom is a rare resource. It'll be a huge waste to use it all for the bait... I'll adjust the portions to make sure the bait is just poisonous enough to weaken the Scorpion but not kill it.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: There's also a third method... Not a clever one though. We risk our lives to hunt it down without any of preparation.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: But this method has its merits, too. It avoids any contamination so that we can extract the purest Scorpion venom.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: I'll leave the final choice to you. Please take your time.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Oh, one more thing. When fighting with the Scorpion, we must be very careful. Its toxin can be lethal.

choices.text: Let's use the paralyzing poisonous bait.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Very well... Are there any cuts or scratches on your hands?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tadhla prepares the poisonous bait carefully as you wait patiently in the cave until the moon rises...

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: It's working. Let's go!

choices.text: Let's use the viper venom bait.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Be careful and don't cut yourself. It'll be a disaster if viper venom gets into your body.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tadhla prepares the poisonous bait carefully as you wait patiently in the cave until the moon rises...

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: It has been weakened. Let's go!

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Then I will watch your back.

talks.objective: Conceal yourself in the hiding place

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: We need to wait patiently... They should've smelled the blood, but they won't be active before the night falls.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: ...Thank you. You didn't have to do this for me.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: I'm fine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You are bleeding...

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: It's nothing. Just a scratch.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Alright... Next up, dissection.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Pfft...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? What's so funny?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Pretty uncommon for a Falcon, I would say.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: It's just... It's kind of funny when you suddenly asked to see how I dissect the Scorpion.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: I barely know anyone else who is as interested in taking apart prey as you are. Or are you interested in this for some other reason?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm just worried that your hands might shake.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: They do not shake when I hunt. Nor will they shake when I harvest my prey.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: No need to worry. I am a "Falcon," after all...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tadhla slowly cuts the Scorpion open, harvests its poison glands, and removes the useless organs, and carefully wraps them up in separate packages.\nWhile doing this, her hands are nimble and steady, as if playing a soundless musical instrument that is made of blood and chitin.\n...It is only a short while before she finishes the dissection.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After all this work, Tadhla lets out a long breath.\nHer forehead is dotted with tiny beads of sweat, her breaths tremulous... Her fresh wound must really hurt.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: See? It's just a scratch. For a Falcon, it's nothing to worry about.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Alright, we still need to hunt the Flying Serpent. Let's go.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: No... If not preserved properly, the poison glands will spoil in the air and become useless.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tadhla harvests the Scorpion with ease, removing its poison glands and useless organs, then carefully wraps them up in separate packages.\nAfter that, she shows you her stained hands without a change of expression on her face. Somehow you feel that she is trying to prove something to you...

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: No... Um... Just a little bit, but it doesn't matter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't push yourself too hard.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: I won't. Thank you, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Wait... I feel it... The familiar... pain.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: It is my soul, my fragments... One is around here...

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: This place is a habitat for flying serpents. Seems this oasis is powered by one of the Jinni's fragments and has become an ecosystem for them...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: That's right. Uh... No, I can't sense the fragment due to the interference of the flying serpents here. Their scents are too thick, too pungent...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then let's go deep and take them down!

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Yes...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: I guess you wanted to say "Let's go!" but you'd better stand down and take a break.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: ...I'll check the Flying Serpent up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tadhla! Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: *pant* Yes...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: She means to say that "It hurts."

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: I... Do not...

choices.text: It's okay. Let me do it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, you should get some rest!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yes, from now on, you can totally count on us! Umm, Paimon means you can totally count on {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Sorry for not being helpful...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't say that, you deserve some rest! There's nothing wrong with us helping out when you're not feeling so well. We're friends after all!

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: I am but a Falcon of Masseira's.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Fine.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ah... Pardon me, my master, but I... sense my fragment nearby.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: ...It's okay. I'll go take care of our prey.

choices.text: We see you only as our friend.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Thank you.

talks.objective: Talk after defeating the Flying Serpent
Let the Jinni open the stone wall

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As the shard of light merges with Liloupar's magic bottle, you feel a little of your own power being pulled away...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Through the Jinni's entranced eyes, you see a vortex of decay and betrayal...\nThe Spirit of Victory fell into madness due to a signet ring most dark, and in a series of tragedies, Queen Shirin brewed the honey-colored catastrophe before her mind yielded to hysteria...\nThe people turned against each other, and the Jinn scattered across the lands... Broken souls became fuel to a titanic machine, and the mindless descendants of the Seelie were degraded into slaves of infinite power...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Then, the merciless era of the Spirit of Victory began... The crazed king and the nobles rejoiced in their superiority...\nYet none were aware that all the happenings within Gurabad were created by the scheming hands of the Mother of the Jinn...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: My master, are you feeling alright?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Apologies. Experiencing a Jinni's memories is not necessarily always a pleasant experience.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Liloupar, what have you done...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: What have I done? You should see what they have done... With just a nudge, they would have cast themselves down the vile path toward certain ruination.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: The fall of Gurabad... is just a prologue. I merely revealed what torments await.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Alright, now is not the time for such a topic... Your friends are waiting for you to wake up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you awake? Can you not always scare Paimon to death!?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Oh, you are finally awake. Paimon was so worried about you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So was Tadhla! When you fell unconscious, she was really nervous and almost cried! Paimon thinks you owe Tadhla an apology!

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: I was not...

choices.text: I didn't mean to make you worry, Tadhla. I'm sorry.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: A hunter does not apologize to a Falcon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How is your wound now?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Hmm... It's been better. Let's head back.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: She's shaking, as if having a fever... It's the Scorpion's toxin. I know it well.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: It is not lethal. But the effects are still deleterious in pain and harm... She will need to rest.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: No need. I'm okay.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: For now, perhaps. Yet, time is like a fraying blade in the desert. Soon, the toxins and the heat will unite against your flesh, inflicting dehydration, and drawing you closer to the rapids of demise.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: A good Falcon knows to cherish their life. Or they will become a burden and be eliminated. Be you a foolish Falcon, child?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's enough, Liloupar. Don't be so harsh to her! And Tadhla, stop treating yourself this way... We really should get some rest before we go!

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Ah... I'm sorry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There is no need to apologize! This cave should be able to block out the cold winds at night. Let's set up a campfire right here!

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Good idea... Let me help... *grunt*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we got this. We're experts when it comes to building a campfire!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You build a simple campfire and cook some food together with Paimon.\nTadhla drinks some water and falls asleep soon...\nHer body is mildly over-warm. Under the influence of the dehydration and fatigue inflicted by the Scorpion's venom, Tadhla sinks into a deep slumber. You can tell that the pain is wearing off on her...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After some time, the morning sun lights up the scarlet desert...\nThe sun is up, and you all wake up as the morning dew dries up in sunlight's heat.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Time to get up. Let's go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You look a lot better, Tadhla. How are you feeling?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: I'm feeling much better now... Come on, let's go.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Pretty soon the day will be searing hot under the sun. If we want to return to the tribe safe and sound, we need to go now.

choices.text: Please don't push yourself too hard.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: It's nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: We are back. This is the prey you asked for.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: A little later than I expected. What happened, my little Falcon?

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: It's embarrassing to say. I... I got injured. But thanks to the Master of the Jinni, I'm okay now.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Good, very good. It's good to see you're alright.

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Esteemed Master of the Jinni, did my Falcon hold you back?

choices.text: Tadhla has done me a big favor.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Is that so...

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Very well. Thank you very much.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: But... Falcons belong to hunters, not the earth. Once Falcons get attached to the world, their senses and claws will be dull. If that happens, how can I expect them to hunt for me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That doesn't make any sense to Paimon... But hearing you going on and on about Falcons surely makes Paimon irritated!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Tadhla is human, and our friend! Not some sort of so-called "Falcon"!

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: "Friend," huh?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: No... It's not like that...

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: I will deal with you later.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Haha, please, don't get me wrong! I am most happy that my little Falcon has made some new friends! Truly, I am.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Here, this is your payment. Please do come find me later. I'll probably have other commissions for you.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: My little Falcon, let's talk about your next "hunt," shall we?

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Oh, a great time?

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Very well. Thank you very much.

choices.text: Please do not have such doubts. Tadhla is extremely capable.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: I know that, of course. She's my Falcon, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Hello, thank you for your help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tadhla! Looks like you're in better spirits now! How's your wound now? Has it healed?

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Thank you for asking. Yes, it has healed... but left an indelible scar.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: No need to worry about me. Master... I mean, my father must have given you this commission.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: There are three targets for this hunt: the Red Vulture, the Scorpion, and the Flying Serpent.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: First, the Red Vulture. We have already confirmed its whereabouts. All that needs to be done is to track it down.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: But of course, if you have other priorities, I'll wait here until you're all set. Only the prey won't be as patient as I am...

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Please follow me.

choices.text: I have to finish something else first.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Don't worry, I'll be here waiting for you.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: That's not the target for this hunt. My apologies.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Tadhla fetches some desert poplar branches and dried feces. Soon, a simple campfire is built.\nSitting and bathing in its warm light, you all share filling quantities of food and water with each other.\nWatching the campfire dancing and crackling, you find yourselves absent of any topics to discuss...

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Ah, esteemed master of the Jinni! And eh... Hmm. I see you have both returned.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Hand over the prey)

dialogues.speaker: Masseira
dialogues.text: Ah, the distinguished Master of the Jinni. If you are here for Tadhla, it might not be a convenient time.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: I am her Father, she is my Falcon. Although she is not the only Falcon that has grown up under my tutelage, she is the one that I trust the most.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Trust is invaluable. It is something that concerns life and death in this tribe.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: I am a hunter in the tribe, but I'm getting old and not as strong and agile as before... In time, your friend Jeht will take the place of old timers like me.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: So, I have high hopes for Tadhla. When the day comes that I have to retire, I need to have at least one Falcon that I can trust.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: Tanit is our tribe, our home.

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: In the desert, no one can survive without the protection of the tribe. Also, if the tribe needs to take someone's life, how can they escape under the omnipresence of the "eyes" and "claws" of our Falcons?

response.speaker: Masseira
response.text: May patterns on the sand dunes guide your way, esteemed Master of the Jinni.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Did you finish dealing with the Jinn matter?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Please don't worry about me. I'm still busy with something...

choices.text: How is your wound? Is it getting better?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Yes, it doesn't hurt anymore. *grunt* It's okay now.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Hello, the Master of the Jinni.

choices.text: How is your wound? Is it getting better?

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Nothing to worry about. No need to worry about me.

response.speaker: Tadhla
response.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Please follow me. We have already confirmed its whereabouts. All that needs to be done is to track it down.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: By the way, are you wearing any perfume?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, why'd you ask?

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Great, neither am I.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: I can smell the lair. Yes, it is right there.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Well then, let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Paimon, you've been holding your nose the whole time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Because it stinks of blood...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: But all the scents that greet me are from wild creatures... Ah, it is not so foul.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, speaking of which, where "is" your nose?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Hmph, be silent...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tadhla, you don't look so well. Do you need some rest?

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Falcons get injured, too. There's no need to be ashamed of such facts, little one.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: I'm not.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... Easy peasy! Paimon didn't even break a sweat!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? What's wrong, Tadhla? Are you still feeling unwell?

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: No, I'm great.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Should you bear words, give them unto my master now.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: I... I am very happy to hunt with you.

dialogues.speaker: Tadhla
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Well... that's a first for a Falcon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... The Red Vulture won't be back anytime soon. Why don't we check out the <color=#00E1FFFF>shiny stuff</color> first?
